dedupe_keys.name: gmie global maximum irrigation extent and central pivot irrigation system dataset

description: GMIE maps the global maximum extent of irrigation at 100-metre resolution together with a global dataset of centre-pivot irrigation systems (GCPIS). Irrigated land is detected from crop performance under drought stress with a machine-learning method: dry months of 2017 to 2019 are used where irrigation is regular and the driest months of 2010 to 2019 where it is occasional. GMIE-100 is a set of 67 GeoTIFF tiles, each pixel giving the irrigated proportion of its cell from 0 to 1, and the centre pivots are shapefiles. It was produced at the Aerospace Information Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and published on Harvard Dataverse as a free download under CC0 (released 2023, latest version February 2025). Caveats: it represents a maximum extent, not irrigation in a given year, and the method depends on drought signals being present. Simulation uses: irrigated area and centre-pivot infrastructure for irrigation capacity planning and drought adaptation. Related records: GMIA-NEXT (data-gmia-next-global-irrigated-areas-30m) and the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas).
name: GMIE global maximum irrigation extent and central pivot irrigation system dataset
